newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: TAURO BANK TO MAKE 40 MLN LITAS SHARE ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: TAURO BANK TO MAKE 40 MLN LITAS SHARE ISSUE.

text.p: Lithuania's Tauro Bank said on Friday that its shareholders had decided to make a 40 million litas issue which will boost its share capital to 76 million litas.
The bank said in a statement that the issue would be open as it is seeking to have itself listed on the country's bourse.
"We have decided to change our status from a limited liability company to a publicly listed company," Rasa Shereniene, the bank's deputy chairwoman, told Reuters.
She also said that the bank hoped to list its current 36 million litas in share capital on the bourse in May.
She added that the bank hoped to distribute the new share 40 million litas share issue among foreign investors.
"The bank already has several prospective buyers," she said but declined to name them.
The bank said that its 1996 net profit was 10.6 million litas versus a loss of 16.8 million litas in 1995.
It also said that the shareholders' meeting decided to use all of the profit for further developments in the bank and not to pay dividends.
The medium-sized bank, the seventh largest in the country interms of assets, said that its liquidity ratio was 61.5 percent at the end of 1996 while its capital adequacy was 17.8 percent.
Both figures are well above the minimum requirements set by the country's central bank.
